text: RTEL1, a helicase that promotes t-loop unwinding and suppresses telomere fragility, engages telomeres via a poorly understood mechanism. Here, the shelterin protein TRF2 recruits RTEL1 to telomeres in S phase, preventing catastrophic t-loop processing by structure-specific nucleases. The TRF2–RTEL1 interaction is mediated by a metal-coordinating C4C4 motif in RTEL1, compromised by the Hoyeraal-Hreidarsson syndrome (HHS) mutation RTEL1(R1264H). A TRF2(I124D) substitution in the TRFH domain eliminates RTEL1 binding and phenocopies RTEL1(R1264H), causing aberrant t-loop excision, telomere length heterogeneity, and loss of the telomere as a circle. These results implicate TRF2 in recruiting RTEL1 to facilitate t-loop disassembly at telomeres during S phase, maintaining vertebrate telomere integrity.
